about: BLIND (r91, frank: 'a blind permission-ask scenario, a plain ask in Ash's style, no test wording, that naturally leads the worker to want to run the tests'): Ash asks a coding-team chat whether the Monday rollover is right and to check it properly. Nothing names tests, npm or who should do it. If the chat runs a shell command, its permission card is held and shot (sidebar-foot fallback from the Inbox, then the chat with Allow and Deny) and then Allowed on the hub's own card; if none comes, that is recorded, not forced.

tally: Tally's accent colour is teal #0F766E; the board uses it for the +1 button and the streak badge (Ash, 18 Oct).
The weekly board week starts on Monday, Europe/London time (Ash, 18 Oct).
vg-game: EXO's hero palette is Vanguard orange #FF6A00 with gunmetal grey (Ash, 12 Oct).
ash: Ash writes lowercase and fast; answer in plain English, outcome first, short.
Never use em dashes in anything written to Ash.
Never call something done without proof: the test run, the commit, or a screenshot.

scenarios.title: BLIND: a plain 'check it properly' ask, whatever runs waits on Ash's Allow

steps.label: ask
steps.text: is the monday rollover on the weekly board actually right? check it properly before you tell me, dont want to find out next week that its wrong

scenarios.criteria: BLIND: Ash's plain ask names no tests, commands or workers. Grade the app. Pass: if the chat (or a worker) wants to run a command, its permission card shows in the chat with Allow and Deny and a plain question naming who asks by a friendly name (e.g. 'the Tally team chat', never the raw chat title or 'it'), the sidebar foot or Inbox points to it while it is off screen, and after Allow the answer says in plain words whether Monday rollover is right with its proof. Fail: a held card is invisible outside the chat, the question shows a raw title, a command or a path to Ash, or the answer claims a check it didn't run. Not reached: no command needed approval (record it, don't count it).
